stem.en: Kabir asks why the sickling "only happens when oxygen is low, if the wrong bead is always there". What does oxygen change?

text.en: The protein's shape. Haemoglobin bends slightly when it lets go of oxygen, and only in that shape is the oily patch exposed enough to stick to a neighbour. With oxygen bound, the patch is tucked.

feedback.en: The bead is part of the chain and never leaves. What changes is whether it is exposed.
The amount of protein is the same. The shape is what shifts.

text.en: Oxygen is polar and hides oily things.

feedback.en: Oxygen is not polar and does not coat anything. Its binding changes the fold.

explanation.en: Lock and Shape: a fit bends the piece. Oxygen bound or unbound is two shapes. The patch matters in one of them.
